subject: sarf
definition: A verb or noun made only of its root letters, with no added letter.
explanation: Most verbs have three root letters (thulāthī): نَصَرَ، ضَرَبَ، فَتَحَ. A few have four (rubāʿī), such as دَحْرَجَ (he rolled). In the bare form, the past tense of the third person has only these letters.

The bare three-letter verb comes in six patterns (abwāb), named by the vowel of the ʿayn in the past and in the present: نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ، ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ، فَتَحَ يَفْتَحُ، سَمِعَ يَسْمَعُ، كَرُمَ يَكْرُمُ، حَسِبَ يَحْسِبُ. Which pattern a verb takes is learnt by hearing it, not by a rule.

examples.english: naṣara yanṣuru: a in the past, u in the present.
samiʿa yasmaʿu: i in the past, a in the present.
